page.title: Sulphide Del Rey Campground
page.text: Breadcrumb Forest Service Home Southwestern Region Tonto National Forest Recreation Sulphide Del Rey Campground T T T Alerts Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Tours Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Recreation Region: Globe Ranger District Sulphide Del Rey Campground Sulphide Del Rey was once a site of an old mining company. The miners lived here to escape the heat of the lower elevations where they worked during the day. This site offers an exciting place to camp with the family because of the ponderosa pine and abundance in wildlife. General Information Seasons of Use Open Season: Year round Operational Hours Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m. Restrictions Restrictions 14-day stay limit. Only trailers under 20 feet allowed. Fire in designated areas only - and only when fires are allowed. No trash service. Pack It In, Pack It Out. Dispose of waste properly. Leave what you find. Quiet hours 10:00 pm to 6:00 am (running generators are not permitted during quiet hours). Fee Site and Info No fees are required for this site Office Contact Information Globe Ranger Station Address: 7680 S. Six Shooter, Canyon Rd. Globe, AZ 85501 Phone: 928-402-6200 Hours: Mon.-Fri. 8 a.m.-4:30 p.m. (closed noon to 12:30 p.m.) Passes, permits and products not sold after 4 pm. Closed Saturday and Sunday (Closed on federal holidays ) Getting There Latitude / Longitude Latitude: 33.29278034 Longitude: -110.86806 Elevation 6,000 Feet Directions This site is 9 ¼ miles southwest of Globe, in the Pinal Mountains. From Globe, follow paved Jess Hayes Road southeast to junction of Icehouse Canyon Road/Forest Road (FR) 112 and Sixshooter Canyon Road/FR 22. Continue on FR 112 for 2 ¼ miles to the junction of FR 55 and FR 112. Take the right fork and continue for 2½ miles on FR 55, which soon becomes unpaved. At the junction of FR 55 and FR 651 turn left. Proceed 5 miles to the site. View and download a map. page.title: Haigler Canyon Campground and Day Use
page.text: Breadcrumb Forest Service Home Southwestern Region Tonto National Forest Recreation Haigler Canyon Campground and Day Use T T T Alerts Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Tours Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Recreation Region: Pleasant Valley Ranger District Haigler Canyon Campground and Day Use Haigler Canyon is deep within the forest. The unpaved road is windy, narrow, and steep which makes this recreation site a favorite for OHV use. Families enjoy driving down meandering roads on their OHVs while anglers enjoy fishing for trout at Haigler Creek. Haigler Canyon Trailhead also offers beautiful vistas, peace, and tranquility. Several shaded campsites include designated picnic tables with grills that offer more leisure time for relaxation. This campground was constructed in 2007 and offers 2 independent campground areas with 14 overnight sites. The recreation area also includes 2 picnic sites available for day-use visitors. This campground boasts a diversity of trees. Fishing for rainbow trout is a popular pastime here. The stream is periodically stocked with trout from April through late August. General Information Seasons of Use Year-round Operational Hours Quiet hours are 10:00 p.m. until 6:00 a.m. Restrictions 14-day stay limit. Trailers under 20 feet. FR 200 and 291 are unpaved roads. Four-wheel-drive or chains are advised after heavy rains/snow. Only street-legal OHVs are allowed. Haigler Creek is prone to have flash floods from rains on the Mogollon Rim, only street-legal OHVs are allowed. Bear-proof your camp - especially your food-stuff. In winter, temperatures dip into the teens. PACK IT IN, PACK IT OUT . Quiet hours 10:00 pm to 6:00 am (running generators are not permitted during quiet hours). Fee Site and Info No fees are required for this site Office Contact Information Payson Ranger Station Address: 1009 E. Turn right on Colcord Road 291 and travel 3 miles to FR 200. Turn right on unpaved FR 200. Travel on FR 200 for 6 miles, through Haigler Canyon Recreation Site to FR 202A. Turn right and follow this unpaved road for ½ mile to the site. Access #2 (12 miles north of Young): From Young, travel 3 miles north on State Hwy.288/Forest Road (FR) 512 to FR 200. Turn left on FR 200 and travel for 9 miles to the site. Facility and Amenity Information Restrooms Vault toilet(s) Water Potable water is not available at this site. page.title: Blodgett Campground
page.text: Breadcrumb Forest Service Home Northern Region Bitterroot National Forest Recreation Blodgett Campground T T T Alerts Events Passes Permits Recreation Camping and Cabins Opportunities Discover History Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Site Open Recreation Region: Stevensville Ranger District Blodgett Campground Current Conditions Open May 1 - October 31 Located 6 miles from the town of Hamilton, Montana, Blodgett Campground consists of 5 campsites, 1 walk-in site, plus 1 host site, complete with picnic tables, fire rings, and a vault toilet. There are two accessible campsites. Campground can accommodate tents, RV's or trailers up to 45 feet. Blodgett Canyon Picnic Area is located across the creek from the campground. No fees. Campsites are available on a first come/first served basis. Food Storage Required: Bitterroot National Forest Food Storage Order Camping is limited to 16 consecutive days: Camping Restrictions Regional Order At least one person must occupy a camping area during the first night after camping equipment has been set up, unless permission has otherwise been granted by the Forest Ranger. Camping equipment cannot be left unattended for more than 24 hours without permission by the Forest Ranger. The Forest Service is not responsible for any loss or damage to personal property The campground rests under the towering cliff faces of Blodgett Canyon which are very popular to rock climbers. Blodgett Canyon Trail follows Blodgett Creek into a canyon with views of these spectacular cliffs and spires. Blodgett Campground Sites General Information Bears frequent the area - A Food Storage Order is in effect on all National Forest System lands within the Montana portion of the Bitterroot National Forest from March 1 - December 1 annually. Seasons of Use Memorial Day to Labor Day Operational Hours Campground open 24 hours a day, 7 days week during open operational period. Restrictions Camping is limited to 16 consecutive days. After 16 days, you must move 5 miles away from your camp site, as the crow flies. Quiet hours 10 p.m. – 6 a.m. Pets must be leashed in the campground. Consider leashing dogs at all trailheads the first few miles of the trail to prevent user conflicts in congested areas. No garbage service, pack it in/pack it out. Food Storage Required Campfires allowed depending on Fire Danger level. Ensure your campfire is OUT before you leave. Do not rinse or wash dishes/etc. out of the creek. Do it on land. Respect wildlife Use of fireworks or other explosives is prohibited on all National Forest lands Firing a gun is not allowed in or within 150 yards of a residence, building, campsite, developed recreation site, or occupied area, across or on a road or body of water, or in any circumstance whereby any person may be injured or property damaged. Fee Site and Info No fees are required for this site No fees. Sites are first come, first served. Pet Information Dogs must be kept on leash in the campground. Office Contact Information Stevensville Ranger District Address: 88 Main Street Stevensville, MT 59870 Phone: 406-777-5461 Hours: Monday-Friday, 8:00 a.m. - 4:30 p.m. (Closed on federal holidays ) Getting There Latitude / Longitude Latitude: 46.26972222 Longitude: -114.2441667 Elevation 4,275 feet Directions From Hamilton, Montana go west on Main Street for 1 mile, turn north (right) onto Ricketts Road and travel 0.5 miles. Turn west (left) onto Blodgett Camp Rd/FS 736 and follow approximately 4 miles to the campground. Travel Considerations Campground is typically not accessible in winter months. Facility and Amenity Information Accessibility 2 Campsites are designated as accessible Restrooms Vault toilet(s) Water Potable water is not available at this site. Picnic Tables Picnic tables are available at this site. Horse/Pack Animal Information Horse/Pack animals are not allowed at this site. Campground does not accommodate pack stock. Nearby Trails Blodgett Creek Trail # 19 Blodgett Overlook Trail # 101 Blodgett Pass Trail # 310 Recreation Opportunities Picnicking Picnicking - Single Hiking General Hiking Backpacking Day Hikes Fishing Fishing - River/Stream Fishing - River/Stream Info Blodgett Creek offers a secluded fishing experience along with scenic beauty. Blodgett Creek is home to Rainbow, Cutthroat, and Brown trout. Blodgett Canyon Trail follows the creek, offering both hiking and fishing opportunities. Be sure to check with the Montana Fish, Wildlife, and Parks regulations for any specific fishing rules or regulations for Blodgett Creek. There are several local fly shops in Hamilton that can provide the best suggestions. Be aware of potential flooding during certain times of the year, especially in the upper reaches of the trail. Paradise Campground is located near the Paradise Boat Launch site for the permitted Selway River, May 15- July 31st annually. The campground consists of 6 sites complete with picnic tables, and fire rings. Other facilities include 3 vault toilets, hitching rails, and feed bunks. Campground can accommodate RV's or trailers to 25 feet. Paradise Campground Sites located at Paradise Campground General Information Paradise campground is used by stock users and hikers alike. This campground is at the end of the road, and many trails depart from this location. Stock is welcome in this campground. The campground lies on the banks of White Cap Creek, and 1/2 mile from the junction of the Selway River put in. Seasons of Use Summer and fall. The main Forest Roads are not plowed in the fall and winter; Nez Perce Pass will generally get snow first in early fall. Restrictions Quiet Hours 10:00 pm to 6:00 am No shooting in and around the campground. Pack it in, Pack it out, no garbage service provided. https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/alerts.title: Canyon Lake Drawdown Public Safety Closure
https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/alerts.text: Breadcrumb Forest Service Home Southwestern Region Tonto National Forest Alerts Canyon Lake Drawdown Public Safety Closure T T T Alerts Passes Permits Recreation Safety and Outdoor Ethics Visitor Maps and Guides Canyon Lake Drawdown Public Safety Closure Due to the Canyon Lake drawdown all recreational sites around Canyon Lake including the marina and the lakebed will be closed. Apache Trail (SR 88) will remain open. Alert Start Date: September 8, 2026 Alert End Date: February 28, 2027 Order Number: 03-12-00-26-22 Contact Information Contact Name: Mesa Ranger District Contact Number: (480) 610-3300 Associated Documents Closure Order Map Forest Order PROHIBITIONS Pursuant to 16 U.S.C. § 551 and 36 C.F.R. § 261.50 (a) and (b), the following are prohibited on the National Forest System (NFS) lands and roads in the Mesa and Tonto Basin Ranger Districts, Tonto National Forest, described in detail below and shown on the attached map incorporated into this Order as Exhibit A (the “Described Area and Roads”): Going into or being upon the Described Area. 36 C.F.R. § 261.53(e) Being on any road within the Described Area. 36 C.F.R. § 261.54(a). EXEMPTIONS Pursuant to 36 C.F.R. § 261.50(e), the following persons are exempt from this Order: Persons with Forest Service form FS-7700-48, Permit for Use of Roads, Trails, or Areas Restricted by Regulation or Order, specifically exempting them from this Order or a written determination by a Forest Service authorized officer that a permit is not required under 36 C.F.R. § 251.50(e)(1) or (2). Any Federal, State, or Local Officer, or member of an organized rescue or firefighting resource in the performance of an official duty. DESCRIBED AREA/ROADS/TRAILS Starting at the western point of Canyon Lake where Highway 88 first approaches the shoreline, identified at reference point (33° 32.594’N, -111° 26.649’W): From the lakebed to the north edge of Highway 88, follow the paved edge of Highway 88 approximately 1.5 miles along the road as it approached First water Creek cove (First Water Bridge). Continuing south around the lakebed of First Water Creek cove approximately 0.75 miles and returning to Highway 88, crossing back to the north edge of the road. Following north edge of Highway 88 approximately 1.25 miles eastward to site host entrance lane at Boulder Recreation Site, crossing the road and turning south to include the west Boulder Recreation Site boundary. Continuing south beyond the recreation site boundary approximately 0.85 miles along lakebed of La Barge Creek cove to Point B (33° 31.475’N, -111° 25.174’W). Then extending north approximately 0.25 miles to meet Point C on the Boulder Canyon Trail, 103 (33° 31.658’N, -111° 25.178’W). Proceeding northward along the western edge of Trail 103 (not include Trail 103) approximately 0.5 miles until it crosses back over to the north side of Highway 88 across the front of the Canyon Lake Marina entrance. From the Canyon Lake Marina, continue eastward approximately 2.15 miles along Highway 88 to the entrance for Tortilla Campground, then moving directly across the wash to the northwest side of the lakebed in Tortilla Creek. Following the lakebed edge of Tortilla Creek northwest approximately 1.35 miles back to the main lakebed of Canyon Lake. Back at Canyon Lake westward along the north shore of Canyon Lake winding west then turning northeast following the south side of the Salt River’s southern edge to the base of Horse Mesa Dam approximately 12.25 miles. Crossing with Horse Mesa Dam, then returning southwest along the Salt River’s northern edge to Canyon Lake approximately 11 miles to Mormon Flat Dam. From Mormon Flat Dam, crossing to the south shore of the lakebed and returning southwest approximately 1.15 miles back to point of beginning at Highway 88, 33° 32.594’N, -111° 26.649’W. FEATURES IN OR AROUND THE DESCRIBED AREA Closed Road: National Forest System Road 80 from Highway 88 approximately 6 miles north to its terminus is closed. Closed Interior Recreation site Roads: Forest Roads 147, 148, 150, 164, 164A, 1825, 1826, 256, 256B, 3434, 3442, 3543. Closed Recreation Sites: Acacia, Palo Verde, Boulder, Canyon Lake Marina, Laguna, Tortilla Campground. Open Boundary Roads/Trails: SR 88 and Trail # 103 Boulder. PURPOSE The purpose of this Order is to protect public health and safety from unstable exposed shoreline features and unsafe lakebed surface conditions as Canyon Lake waters recede during the planned Salt River Project (SRP) planned drawdown. NFSR 80 is closed to protect the public from a high volume of construction vehicles being used for SRP construction maintenance at Fish Creek near Horse Mesa Dam. IMPLEMENTATION This Order shall be in effect from September 8, 2026, at 6 a.m. through February 28, 2027, at 6 p.m., unless rescinded. A map identifying the Described Area and Roads is attached and made part of this Order as Exhibit A. For a digital version of this Order and Exhibit A, go to https://www.fs.usda.gov/r03/tonto/alerts Unless otherwise expressly defined in this Order, the terms used in this Order are defined by the regulations of the Secretary of Agriculture, 36 C.F.R. Chapter II, Parts 200-299. If there are terms in this Order that are not expressly defined in the Order or 36 C.F.R. Chapter II, Parts 200-299, their meaning shall be determined by their plain language definitions. A violation of the above prohibitions is punishable as a Class B misdemeanor by a fine of not more than $5,000 for individuals and $10,000 for organizations, or by imprisonment for not more than six months, or both. 16 U.S.C. § 551; 18 U.S.C. §§ 3559, 3571, and 3581. Contact the Mesa Ranger District in Mesa, AZ (480) 610-3300 or Tonto Basin Ranger District in Roosevelt, AZ (602) 225-5395 for more information about this Order. This Order supersedes any previous Orders prohibiting the same or similar acts in/on the same Described Area and Roads. Signed and issued on August 25, 2026.
